title: Config safety umbrella: automated recovery, cost-aware batching suggestions, and state harmonization
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Goal: Build an automated recovery layer ("safety umbrella") that 1) detects harmful configuration changes to serving/runtime and applies safe remediation automatically, 2) surfaces cost-aware batching/caching recommendations and can opt in to automated conservative config adjustments, and 3) reconciles desired vs actual system state across regions and dedicated pools without causing churn.
background: Multiple incidents in Q4 and Q1 showed that small config flips (batch size, cache TTL, kernel selection flags) can increase unit cost or cause tail latency regressions. We currently have manual playbooks and semi-automated canaries, but teams still need fast, deterministic rollback and suggestions that balance cost vs latency. This ticket unifies detection triggers, a conservative remediation policy, and a reconciliation engine that avoids flip-flopping state across controllers.
scope:
- Implement detection triggers based on cost delta, p50/p95 latency shift, error-rate bump, and model-quality regressions (from eval hooks).
- Define guardrails and a conservative remediation palette (eg. reduce batch size, disable prefetch, switch to cached model variant, revert single-field config to last-known-good).
- Add a recommendations layer that surfaces per-route batching/caching suggestions with estimated cost delta and risk score.
- Implement a state harmonizer that applies changes with hysteresis and write locks to avoid repeated toggles across regions.
- Integrate with Console alerts, rollout engine, and audit logs.
- Provide end-to-end tests and chaos scenarios in staging.
acceptance_criteria: Detection: At least 4 signal types ingested (latency, error rate, token cost, eval drift) and paired into a unified incident trigger with tunable thresholds.
Automated remediation: The system can perform a safe automated action (from the remediation palette) and create an auditable rollback event with root-cause suggestion in Console.
Recommendations: For top 10 customer routes in staging, the system produces batching/caching suggestions with estimated monthly cost delta and a risk score.

Reconciliation: State harmonizer prevents more than 2 config flips on the same target in a 1-hour window during a simulated jitter test and converges to the last-approved desired state within 5 minutes after network partition heal.
Observability: All automated actions create traces, events, and a short human-readable rationale stored in the audit log and surfaced in the rollout UI.
Tests: Unit and integration tests for trigger logic, remediation execution, and reconciliation behavior are included and pass in CI.
design_decisions: Use a policy-first approach: remediation actions are declarative and staged (probe -> conservative apply -> monitor -> escalate).
Keep remediation palette minimal: prefer conservative, reversible actions (eg. lowering batch size by one step) over aggressive model swaps unless explicit consent present.
Recommendations are advisory by default; we will implement an opt-in automated apply flow behind a feature flag for early adopters.
Reconciliation will use an authoritative desired-state store with per-target revision numbers and a leader-election lock to avoid concurrent conflicting writers.
Cost estimates will be derived from token throughput logs and recent kernel/memory profiles; we will surface a 95% confidence band rather than single-point estimates.
implementation_notes: Signals ingestion: extend metrics-agent to annotate per-request tokens and kernel type to enable cost deltas by model variant.
Trigger scoring: create a lightweight scoring service that normalizes signals and exposes an API for the remediation controller.
Remediation controller: small state machine with actions: NOOP, APPLY_CONSERVATIVE, ROLLBACK_PREVIOUS, ESCALATE_MANUAL. Actions must be idempotent.
Hysteresis: implement cooldown windows with exponential backoff for repeated flips; store last-action timestamp in durable store (DynamoDB/Postgres).
Audit and trace: every automated event posts to audit logs, creates a Console timeline event, and opens a GitHub PR skeleton for any config diff that requires manual approval.
Feature flags: gate automated apply behind ff://config.safety.automated_apply and per-org allowlist.

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Automated apply may increase churn or hide underlying regressions. Mitigation: start as advisory; automated apply default off; require org opt-in and conservative action set.
Risk: Bad cost estimates leading to poor recommendations. Mitigation: show confidence intervals and require acceptance for >10% projected savings actions.
Risk: Reconciliation flip-flop hitting different control planes (hosted vs dedicated). Mitigation: per-deployment leader locks and region-aware cooldowns.
Risk: Security/audit concerns for automated changes. Mitigation: full audit trail, signed events, and optional SSO approval flow for enterprise orgs.
monitoring_metrics: auto_remediation.count: number of automated actions performed by type
auto_remediation.success_rate: fraction that resolved the trigger without escalation
config_flip.rate: frequency of config changes per target per hour
estimated_cost_delta.monthly_usd: aggregated estimated monthly cost impact of recommendations
time_to_converge.seconds: time for desired vs actual state to match after heal
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (internal): Advisory-only in staging; run recommendations for 2 weeks and validate estimates - small internal group
Phase 1 (pilot): Opt-in orgs (<=5) enable automated conservative remediations with full audit logs - monitor for 2 weeks
Phase 2 (widen): Add more orgs and guardrails (confidence thresholds); expose UI toggles in Console
Phase 3 (GA): Turn on for all hosted accounts with opt-out and enterprise controls; offer dedicated-deployment adapters separately
